source: So many primed traps lying in wait, so little time!
My lord, I know now that you murdered your brother.
Come now, Ophelia. Where did you hear a thing like that?
My dear, I am so terribly sorry to hear about the brutal murder of your father.
I heard they only just found his corpse.
And I see that you are mad with grief. I cannot imagine your suffering.
I would be surprised if anyone would believe any accusation you'd make right now.
I'm not 'insane.' I know it's true, Claudius. And you will pay.
I am a seasoned man, my dear. It will take more than the idle threat of a little girl to make me afraid.
Now, be off. I tire of you.
As I told you before, we'll speak when next we're in private.
I trust you won't divulge this story to anyone else until I've had a chance to explain myself further.
You think that Bernardo's protection earlier makes you invincible?
You are a fool.
So. You intend to... what? To threaten me in public?
No. If you really want to speak about it, let's speak in private.
I'll tell you everything there. Yes, the truth.
I'll even have Bernardo accompany you for safety, if that puts your mind at ease.
Come now, love. Where did you hear a thing like that?
Ophelia, if I have but one request of you, it is this.
I wish to forget everything which happened before you came to comfort me. All of it.
All the things I did for her--
No. Let this be a new blank world we can impress ourselves upon anew.
Otherwise, if I start to think about it--
I might break.
So never ask me about the past. It doesn't matter any more. And it never shall.
My lady, I have unfortunate news about your husband's role in King Hamlet's death.
Closer, Ophelia, and lower your voice. Please.
What are you saying?
I believe King Hamlet was murdered, my lady. I overheard Claudius confessing it himself.
King Hamlet wasn't bitten by a snake at all.
I don't understand. What are you saying?
Please tell me this is a sick joke of yours.
B-because, if it's true—
I know it's difficult to hear, my lady.
Could Claudius have...
I understand you may have seen something you can't describe, Ophelia, but you must have been mistaken.
I'm certain Claudius didn't mean whatever he said. Or perhaps you heard it out of context.
Regardless, I shall seek him out myself and clear the air. I'll clarify that it was nothing after all.
Frankly, I had thought this kind of whisper-trading beneath you, Ophelia.
Laertes, I overheard the King confessing he murdered his brother.
What? You're certain?
Yes. He was in the chapel. I heard him praying.
You're absolutely certain? Ophelia, this is the kind of accusation which gets both of us killed.
I'm certain. I saw it with my own eyes. Hamlet was there, too.
As much as I hate to admit it, I believe you.
After King Hamlet died, there were cruel rumors like that... but to have heard a confession is something else altogether.
Normally I'd turn to Lady Brit in matters like these, but I've done so once already, and it was clear that it troubled her greatly.
I'll have to think upon an alternative solution. Deal with this on my own.
A confession from my own blood is as good as truth to me.
Now, I shall take what must be taken.
I think I know who to turn to for rumormongering of this sort.
Lady Brit is one of the best. If other accounts of this kind of thing exist, she'd know.
And that might be the support we need.
You haven't heard the news?
What news?
Ah... never mind it.
(He'll find out soon enough.)
In the past, I would have turned to Brit for something like this. But -- well.
Now I don't know where to go.
I will not be made gutless. I will not wait.
Many have long suspected this King's treachery. Now, you confirm it.
Hamlet, I know that Claudius murdered your father.
I saw him confess myself. The truth is undeniable now.
But it took so much for me to be sure. I no longer know what to do. And now everything's become stranger than before.
What? You... know this?
It's hard to explain, but I... heard him confessing it himself.
He was praying, and he stated it plainly, without poetry.
And now he's dust.
I hope he's burning in Hell.
I thought I was alone in this.
You're the only other person who suspects him.
Now is the time. You have to do something, Hamlet.
If he truly confessed before you, then that's the proof I need to act.
Were it coming from anyone but you, Ophelia, I could scarce believe it.
My uncle must die. What a relief it is to feel that for certain.
My father's spirit told me precisely what you've just said. That my uncle killed my father and covered up his crime.
And now you've confirmed it for me. How wonderfully freeing it feels.
For my own sanity, I must find out if my mother knew of this. I have to know if she was complicit, too.
How might we uncover that?
Her journal.
My mother keeps a diary in her bedroom, detailing her every thought. She writes in it often. I thought she might speak of her guilty mind there, if she had one.
She's always been fond of you. You can get into her chambers.
If she was part of this, I have to know for certain. Help me. Please.
If you help me find the diary, I'll take you to meet my father's spirit. Then you'll see that I'm not insane.
And my mother... she willingly betrayed my father for Claudius.
Were she to tell me now that she never suspected him, I wouldn't believe her for an instant.
No. She's as rotten as he. The both of them need to be exposed.
No. Plans have changed. I've something special in mind for the both of them, now.
Hamlet, please, think carefully...
It's too late for me to do something public about this-- to expose them for who they are, on stage...
Bernardo, I have proof that King Claudius murdered his own brother.
We both do, now.
But what am I to do? I cannot take a King into custody.
Even if he shouted it from every rooftop, it would take the will of the nobility to stop him.
...Nevertheless, I thank you. Because you see me for who I am, I was able to stand up to him.
For the first time in my life, I feel entirely drained of fear. He has no control over me anymore.
And despite the dire circumstances we're in, I cannot help but feel like the future is a brighter one.
So thank you, Ophelia. Thank you for standing with me.
This isn't a joke.
Then how did you come to hear such a rumor?
I heard him confess it when he thought he was alone. He was praying.
We suspected, after King Hamlet died. Or at least, my men and I did.
But the physician who attended the body said nothing to us of murder.
Regardless, he has power over me.
He knows that I am also Katherine.
And he would use it against me in an instant if he thought it would benefit him.
But you don't need to be afraid. You have me standing by you. And I'm sure others would, too.
And my thanks for that. But even if that's true...
I cannot arrest a King.
I know now that King Claudius killed his own brother.
This is why I'm smart enough to stay out of court affairs.
I wish I could say I was surprised. But knowing him? Look at him. The man's a nervous wreck.
Something broke him. That must've been it.
I saw King Claudius confess to killing his brother before my own eyes.
Such a chilling message before we've even been acquainted.
I am a man of manners. Please, excuse me. Are you that one they call Lady Ophelia? It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance. I am Othello.
Regardless, as to what you asked about...
I am unsurprised.
Snakes beget snakes. From what I've heard, the King's father was a ruinous man.
He was savage on the battlefield, but, I'm told, even crueler as a King. He took anything he wanted, killed any who disobeyed. Even family.
I've served many a King in battle, but I could never serve one like these.
Not for all the gold in the world.
Father, did you know that King Claudius murdered King Hamlet?
Where did you hear that? Who have you been speaking with?
Is it true?
Do you want to see me killed? Or you? Or your brother?
I tried to tell you before what a delicate situation we... I... am in.
Please, don't do anything to bring public embarrassment to us.
Your brother is already dead. Do you want to see me lose my head, too?
Ophelia, don't you understand how dire things are at the moment?
Father, I heard the King himself confess. I saw him with my own eyes.
You mean to tell me that the King, who is in good health and of sound mind, confessed a murder before your eyes? When? And where?
Yes! In the chapel!
Oh... dear.
I realize what this is. You... you've been listening to the Prince's insane ravings, haven't you?
Be truthful. Did you hear all this from him? Did he ask you to come lie to me?
No! Father, please, believe me!
I've heard enough. You won't mention this to anyone. Not a soul. Understand?
We never spoke of this treason, and you never heard a thing.
Horatio, please keep this quiet, but... I've learned that King Hamlet's death was no accident. He was murdered.
Do you know anything about this?
That's precisely what the spirit told Hamlet.
He asked me to watch Claudius closely for any hint of-- well, guilt, I suppose.
He feels he needs proof before he can act.
He had asked me to watch Claudius closely for any hint of-- well, guilt, I suppose.
Felt he needed proof before he could act, I suppose. Ah, damn all of this sorry business.
If there were some way you could prove what you heard was true... well, it would be calamity. But good calamity, I think.
What? How did you hear that?
S-so you must've seen... it?
You mean the ghost?
So you did hear?
But there's no way...
I know he spoke to his father's spirit.
Well, go talk to him, then. You'll get nothing more out of me.
And a lot of good it did him, in the end.
What is 'it'?
So you haven't, then.
Horatio. Out with it.
Hmph! You may intimidate Hamlet, but you won't intimidate me. The King would guillotine me for a mere whisper of what you just said.
As such, I am a metaphorical and literal stone wall. You'll get nothing out of me.
